result:
PR #356 is ready for review. Preflight passes, and every fold selftest passes when run one at a time on the merged tree. CI hasn't run yet on the new head, 7882771788.

**Why attempt 1 didn't finish:** it pushed its work, then ended waiting on a background selftest run that died with the session, so the PR stayed in draft. The CI run it pushed also failed one selftest check. That test was added to master after the branch forked, and it looks for the exact words `WOULD FOLD (regression accepted on #91)`. My `(score N)` suffix sat in the middle of them. That's recorded in `docs/lanes/foldflow/NOTES.md`.

**Done this session:**
- **Merged master**, which was 74 commits ahead; the merge was clean. The line now reads `WOULD FOLD (regression accepted on #N) (score S)`, which fixes that failing check.
- **`--exact` for #360**, from the host's request on the PR: `regen_index`'s first index check gets `--exact` only if the merged tree's own `nv2a_index.py check --help` lists it. That makes it correct whichever of #356 and #360 folds first. The check after the rebuild is unchanged.
- **New selftest `75-fold-exact.sh`**: it covers a tree before #360 and a tree after it. Two deliberately broken copies of fold.sh (always pass `--exact`, never pass it) both fail it, so the test does exercise the gate.
- **Selftest results:** 73 30/30, 74 27/27, 75 6/6, 86 47/47, 90 31/31.
- **Fresh read-only `fold.sh list` from this branch** (22:56 PDT, live PRs):
  - #330, #332 and #343 conflict only in the generated index, so they would be repaired.
  - #299, #335 and #352 would fold in one tick.
  - The rest wait for the next tick.
  - At 22:51 PDT, master's fold.sh had logged nine PRs as `waits: one fold per tick`.

**Still missing:** the brief asks for one live instance quoted from `tick.log`. That line can only appear once this PR folds and the host's fold job runs the new fold.sh, so until then the proof is the fixtures plus the read-only list run above. I've said so in NOTES and in the PR body.
